Subject: AcmeHealth POC: intermittent prefetch stalls — triage & temporary config ask

Monica — thanks again for the demo today. Two quick follow-ups after the call:

1) What we saw: during your large-document ingestion tests the stream sometimes stalls for ~3-8s mid-response, then resumes. Repros are intermittent (8-12% of requests during the test window).
2) Attachments: I captured the client-side traces and server-side spans (attached as acme_prefetch_stall_logs.zip and trace_20260825.txt).

Ask: can Platform/Runtime triage whether prefetch (KV / prefix caching) is the likely cause and, if so, enable a temporary account-level mitigation while we investigate (examples: set prefetch_kv_ttl=0 or disable prefetch for the POC traffic). Engineering owners, can you confirm what low-risk knob we can flip quickly?

Proposed MAP (mutual action plan):
- Today: Runtime team looks at spans & hypothesis (kv-ttl mismatch) — owner: Karthik/Dev
- Tomorrow: If hypothesis holds, enable temporary config for Acme test account for the POC window — owner: Dev
- Friday: Joint replay with Acme on 10:00 PT to verify fix — owner: Kimberly/Acme

Monica — are you comfortable with us toggling an account-scoped config during your POC? If so, please reply and we’ll proceed.

Thanks,
Kimberly

Redwood Inference

• Repro window: 10:45–11:30 PT today.
• Input pattern: long patient documents (~18k tokens) followed by a short question prompt.
• Observed behavior: ~10% of streams pause after the first chunk and then continue; we see timeouts in our client at 4s if not resumed.
• We attached a small repro script (we can upload if useful) and the request IDs for the stalls: r-3452, r-3459, r-3471.

We are OK with a temporary toggle for the POC. Please keep us posted and let us know if you need more traces.

Subject: Re: AcmeHealth POC: intermittent prefetch stalls — triage & temporary config ask

Thanks for raising — quick clarifying Qs before we flip any knobs:

1) Is there any correlation with variant routing / model fallback when the stall happens? (Monica — do you see a model swap or anything?)
2) Can Dev/Runtime confirm whether the spans show a KV cache miss immediately before the stall (I can look at the link in related_links if already uploaded).

If the hypothesis is 'KV TTL or stale cache entry causing a short stall', a safe short-term mitigation is to set account-level prefetch_kv_ttl=0 (no prefetching) for the POC traffic and then re-run the suite. That is reversible and low-risk operationally. Dev — can you take point on the triage and, if confirmed, propose the exact config and the rollback plan?

Also add JIRA-SUP-7821 to track the work and let SalesOps know if this requires an exemption to standard POC config change process.

-Logan
Product Manager, Platform
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 26 Aug 2026 08:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: AcmeHealth POC: intermittent prefetch stalls — triage & temporary config ask

Acknowledged — I pulled the spans from the attached trace and see repeated KV cache re-validation around the times Monica called out. Hypothesis: the prefetcher aggressively seeds keys but a small TTL mismatch between prefix eviction and lookup causes a transient wait while the runtime refetches the KV bucket (this shows as a short stall in the transcript stream).

Immediate mitigation we can apply (low-risk):
- Apply account-scoped flag prefetch_kv_enabled=false for AcmeHealth test account for POC windows OR
- Set prefetch_kv_ttl=0 so prefetcher is effectively disabled.

I can make the change for the Acme test account and keep it under a feature-flag so rollback is a single API call. Will need an explicit OK from Sales (Kimberly) and a short maintenance window (5 min) when we flip it. I will also instrument an extra metric (prefetch_disabled_requests) so we can monitor impact.

Plan:
1) Kimberly replies OK — we schedule the toggle (I handle).
2) I flip flag in staging -> verify with small replay -> flip in POC account during agreed window -> monitor 30m -> revert if no improvement or unexpected side effects.

Dev
Dev Patel
